subject: Biotechnology
title: Sustainable Aviation Fuel
description: Learn Sustainable Aviation Fuel in one minute.

hook.text: Aviation produces 2.5% of global CO2 — planes cannot run on batteries, so biotech must make their fuel green.

buildup.text: Sustainable aviation fuel is chemically identical to jet fuel — made from biomass, waste oils, or engineered microbes.

discovery.text: Amyris engineers yeast to produce farnesene — a molecule convertible to jet fuel, diesel, and specialty chemicals.

twist.text: SAF costs two to five times more than fossil jet fuel — airlines need mandates or carbon pricing to justify the premium.

climax.text: The EU mandates 6% SAF by 2030 and 70% by 2050 — regulation drives the bioeconomy when markets alone will not.

punchline.text: Fly on biology — sustainable aviation fuel decarbonizes the sky.

quiz.question: Why is sustainable aviation fuel critical for decarbonizing air travel?
options: Electric batteries can power long-haul flights but are not yet commercially available
Aircraft cannot be electrified for long distances, so drop-in bio-based jet fuel is the only viable alternative
SAF is already cheaper than fossil jet fuel

details.summary: Sustainable aviation fuel is produced from biological feedstocks like used cooking oil, agricultural waste, or algae and can reduce lifecycle carbon emissions by up to 80 percent compared to petroleum jet fuel. It is chemically compatible with existing aircraft engines.
details.whyItMatters: Aviation accounts for about 3 percent of global CO2 emissions and cannot be easily electrified. SAF is currently the only viable path to decarbonizing long-haul aviation while using existing aircraft and airport infrastructure.
takeaways: SAF is a drop-in replacement compatible with current jet engines
Lifecycle carbon reductions reach up to 80 percent versus fossil jet fuel
Production from waste oils and biomass avoids competing with food crops

faq.question: Why can't airplanes simply switch to electric power instead?
faq.answer: Batteries are far too heavy for long-haul flight. Jet fuel contains about 50 times more energy per kilogram than current batteries. Until battery density improves dramatically, sustainable aviation fuel is the only practical way to decarbonize commercial aviation.

faq.question: What feedstocks are used to make sustainable aviation fuel?
faq.answer: Used cooking oil, animal fats, agricultural residues, forestry waste, municipal solid waste, and algal oils are all viable. The HEFA pathway from used oils is most mature. Alcohol-to-jet and Fischer-Tropsch pathways from biomass are scaling up.
